new_rows.claim: **The WZO2 4×4 builder reproduces its artifact byte-for-byte across runs.** A 2026-08-03 rebuild (binary `weizigo-oracle-v2-build f25e615-dirty built 2026-08-03T02:24:49Z`, ReleaseFast) produced SHA-256 `0c3366f07fb33c6f2838ead48ad3080b64dbe55935b87af4f140d81a29e4e15a` (518,123,097 bytes) at `untracked/v02/oracle-4x4-v2.wzo2` — byte-identical to the 2026-08-01 artifact from T212 (commit `144148c`) — across six intervening commits touching the builder's import closure (`fd87f83`, `7609420`, `193fdc6` T226 neighbours/area runtime delegation; `4a598b1` T264 banner + vNN output diversion; `656c6d3` T274 WZO1-writer diversion, off the builder path; `b475533` T273 kernel additions, off the builder path). 31 fixpoint sweeps, converged:true; every per-sweep L_changed/H_changed digit-for-digit identical to the recorded run; root (empty,B) L=+1 H=+16, root (empty,W) L=−16 H=−1; 99,133,036 entries; 24,318,165 groups; DTT 10 sweeps, FAR=0; wall 3,789.4 s, peak RSS 3,887 MB, RUNNER_RC=0. Every WZO2 acceptance check A1–A9 reproduces its baselined cell exactly (fast battery gate PASS; slow sweep BASELINE COMPARISON: PASS). Corollaries: T226's genericNeighbors delegation is behaviour-preserving on this path; the artifact header carries no build stamp (T264's sha/date/dirty banner reaches the log/manifest but not the artifact bytes — `artifact2.Header` has no stamp fields). **Scope: reproducibility of the builder only — NOT value correctness (G3b), NOT the T273 kernel, NOT WZO1.** At CLAIMED: promotion past CLAIMED needs mutation adequacy for the code involved (DIRECTION Amendment 2 edge 5), which this run does not provide.

notes: Verified the Orchestrator's result independently. (1) Both artifacts SHA-256 to 0c3366f07fb33c6f2838ead48ad3080b64dbe55935b87af4f140d81a29e4e15a, 518,123,097 bytes (shasum -a 256, both files in one invocation). (2) Root values and all 39 per-sweep L_changed/H_changed lines (31 sweeps + 8 duplicated reprints) match docs/evidence/ORACLE-V2/build-T184-2026-08-01.stdout digit-for-digit (paste-diff, zero differences). Note the prior-artifact lineage: T184 OOM'd at 4473 MB during the write phase and produced nothing; the comparison target 0c3366f0 was built by T212 (commit 144148c, 2026-08-01) after the passes-bit fix; T192's artifact was a892d689. (3) No hash difference, so no structural diff was needed; header analysis (artifact2.Header = w,h,ko_bits,n_groups,n_entries,sha256 only; builder zeroes the sha slot before buildFile fills it) explains why byte-identity holds despite different binaries. (4) Acceptance per-check on the NEW artifact: A1-A9 all PASS with counts identical to the baseline cells, and byte-identical output on the same-instrument control run against the baselined artifact. Fast battery gate PASS via zig build test (exit 0, 43.5 s); slow sweep PASS (BASELINE COMPARISON: PASS) via sh tools/regression-battery-sweep.sh with the deployed binaries. (5) The brief's 'four intervening commits' understates the change: six commits touched the builder's import closure (git log 144148c..f25e615 -- src/oracle_v2_build.zig src/exp6_solve.zig src/rules.zig src/artifact2.zig src/colex.zig), four on the behavioral path; the claim is stronger than the brief stated. (6) Peak RSS 3,887 MB is under both the raised 5,120 MB cap and the standing 4,096 MB cap (209 MB / 5.1% margin) — the standing cap suffices for the CURRENT binary; the T184 OOM (4473 MB, pre-T192-fix code) shows the margin is code-sensitive. (7) NOTED, not acted on: `zig build battery-sweep` currently fails to build because T309's uncommitted src/util.zig rewrite (Threaded-IO replacement) does not compile against Zig 0.16 std.Io.File.writer (22 errors; oracle-v2-accept only — verify-battery does not import util.zig). Worked around by passing the deployed baseline-era binaries directly to the sweep script. Also noted: the deployed oracle-v2-accept is pre-T309 and has the known Threaded-IO stdout-drop bug (T292 F6 / T212 COST-2) — per-check stdout was captured via Python subprocess drain, the same method the baseline used. (8) A rejection of nothing: brief's scope constraints (kernel, G3b, WZO1) were honored and are written into the proposed row. Claims file not edited (T304 owns it); row proposed in findings only.
